content.title: About
content.content: Tomatoes are the edible fruits of the tomato plant (Solanum lycopersicum) cultivated worldwide. Fresh tomatoes are juicy with a mildly sweet‑tart flavor, while cooking softens them and retains most nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Botanically tomatoes are berries, though culinarily they are treated as vegetables.
There are over 10,000 tomato varieties differing in color, shape, and taste.
Lycopene gives tomatoes their red color and is a powerful antioxidant.
Tomatoes were first domesticated in South America more than 7,000 years ago.
They are a major source of the antioxidant lycopene.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains lycopene
items.content: Lycopene has antioxidant properties and may reduce the risk of certain cancers.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Tomatoes are suitable for weight‑management diets due to their low calorie density.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure and supports heart function.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity can aggravate gastritis or heartburn in sensitive people.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Unwashed tomatoes may contain pesticide residues; rinse thoroughly before use.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fresh tomatoes are enjoyed in salads, sandwiches, salsas, and juices. Cooked tomatoes are used in soups, stews, sauces, and casseroles. They can also be roasted, grilled, or steamed.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh tomatoes at room temperature away from direct light for up to 5‑7 days. Cooked tomatoes should be kept in a sealed container in the refrigerator for 3‑4 days. Discard any that become soft, moldy, or develop an off‑odor.
